subject: history
title: Persia, Athens & Alexander
objective: Follow the chain from revolt to empire

lesson.opening: How did resistance to Persia lead into Athenian power and then conflicts among the Greeks?

sections.heading: The institutional thread
sections.body:
Ionian revolt and Persian campaigns

Alliance, tribute, and Athenian empire

Peloponnesian War and Macedonian expansion

sections.heading: A model to test
sections.body: Connect Ionian revolt, mainland intervention, Persian campaigns, allied naval power, tribute, and the rivalry with Sparta. A victory does not explain by itself why the victors later fought one another.

sections.heading: Keep the question
sections.body: How did resistance to Persia lead into Athenian power and then conflicts among the Greeks?

activities.prompt: Which happened first: “Ionian revolt begins” or “Death of Alexander”?
activities.hint: Compare the dates on the unit timeline.

activities.prompt: “Fear of growing Athenian power explains the Peloponnesian War.” — is that an event claim or an interpretation?
activities.hint: This is an influential causal interpretation associated with Thucydides, not simply a date or an observed occurrence.

activities.prompt: Put these events back in chronological order.
Explain the sequence from the Ionian revolt through the Persian invasions without reducing it to a list of battles.
activities.instructions: A few sentences are enough. Cite a passage when it helps.
